title: Asking for Directions
subtitle: Navigating a new city — for English learners

sentences.en: Excuse me, I'm looking for the train station. Is it far?
sentences.target: Excuse me, I'm looking for the train station. Is it far?

sentences.en: It's about a ten-minute walk from here.
sentences.target: It's about a ten-minute walk from here.

sentences.en: Could you show me on my map, please?
sentences.target: Could you show me on my map, please?

sentences.en: Sure. Go straight for two blocks, then take a left at the bank.
sentences.target: Sure. Go straight for two blocks, then take a left at the bank.

sentences.en: After the bank, you'll see a big park on your right.
sentences.target: After the bank, you'll see a big park on your right.

sentences.en: The station is just past the park, across the street.
sentences.target: The station is just past the park, across the street.

sentences.en: Is there a bus I can take instead of walking?
sentences.target: Is there a bus I can take instead of walking?

sentences.en: Yes — the number 14 bus stops right at the station.
sentences.target: Yes — the number 14 bus stops right at the station.

sentences.en: Great, thank you. You've been really helpful.
sentences.target: Great, thank you. You've been really helpful.

sentences.en: No problem. Have a safe trip!
sentences.target: No problem. Have a safe trip!
